# Genprex Presents Preclinical Data Identifying TROP2 as a Potential Predictive Biomarker for Reqorsa® Gene Therapy in Lung Cancer


** November 19, 2026


[Press Releases](https://www.genprex.com/category/press-releases/)[Conferences](https://www.genprex.com/tag/conferences/)[gene therapy](https://www.genprex.com/tag/gene-therapy/)[Reqorsa](https://www.genprex.com/tag/reqorsa/)


*Data Presented at the 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium Show TROP2 Levels May Help Predict Which Tumors Respond to Reqorsa® and Modulating TROP2 May Enhance Efficacy*


AUSTIN, Texas — (Nov. 19, 2026) —[Genprex, Inc.](https://www.genprex.com/) (“Genprex” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ:[GNPX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/gnpx) ), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing gene therapies designed to restore tumor-suppressor function in cancer and insulin-producing function in diabetes, today announced new preclinical data identifying low TROP2 expression as a potential predictive biomarker of primary resistance to its lead drug candidate, Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The findings were presented in a poster titled “TROP2 Predicts Response to TUSC2 Gene Therapy and Its Modulation Sensitizes Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer to Treatment” at the 2026 EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics, taking place November 18-20, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain.


“Identifying which patients are most likely to benefit from REQORSA is one of the most important steps we can take to advance precision oncology,” said Ryan Confer, President and Chief Executive Officer of Genprex. “These data suggest that TROP2 may help us identify which patients will benefit the most from REQORSA. These findings were supported across cell lines, patient-derived organoids and tumor models and in pretreatment biopsies from patients in our clinical program. Additionally, we are encouraged to see that TROP2 may do more than predict patient response. Our collaborators found that modulating TROP2 levels changes how cancer cells responded to REQORSA. We look forward to continuing to explore how TROP2 could help inform patient selection, and even potentially enhance REQORSA treatment, in future studies.”


The TUSC2 tumor suppressor protein expression is downregulated or absent in more than 80% of NSCLC cases and nearly all small cell lung cancers. Previous studies have shown that REQORSA has antitumor activity, including in models resistant to targeted therapies and in immunotherapy-resistant KRAS/LKB1-mutant NSCLC. REQORSA’s effects are mediated by inhibiting MAPK and mTOR signaling, inducing cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis, and activating antitumor immune responses.


Key findings from the research include:


- **Low TROP2 expression associated with resistance** : Approximately 50% of 10 NSCLC cell lines and 50% of 12 patient derived organoid models evaluated showed primary resistance to TUSC2 gene delivery. Protein-expression analyses consistently identified low TROP2 expression as a marker associated with resistance across multiple preclinical models.
- **Supporting clinical evidence:** Analysis of pretreatment tumor biopsies from patients enrolled in a TUSC2 gene therapy clinical trial supported the association between TROP2 expression and treatment response.
- **TROP2 modulation influenced treatment sensitivity:** Introducing TROP2 into TROP2-low NSCLC cells (H460 and H1299) significantly increased TUSC2-induced apoptosis, to levels similar to cells that naturally express high TROP2. Conversely, knocking down or knocking out TROP2 in TROP2-high cells (H358 and H322) using shRNA or CRISPR/Cas9 also significantly increased sensitivity to TUSC2 gene therapy.


Collectively, the findings identify TROP2 as a potential predictive biomarker for response to REQORSA and suggest that modulating TROP2 signaling may be a novel strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of REQORSA in NSCLC. While these findings provide preclinical and supportive clinical evidence, additional research and prospective clinical evaluation will be required to establish TROP2’s predictive utility in patients receiving REQORSA.


The aforementioned poster has been made available on Genprex’s website at[https://www.genprex.com/investors/downloads/](https://www.genprex.com/investors/downloads/) .


**About Reqorsa® Gene Therapy**


Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, consists of a plasmid containing the TUSC2 gene encapsulated in non-viral lipid-based nanoparticles in a lipoplex form (the Company’s Oncoprex® Delivery System), which has a positive charge. REQORSA is injected intravenously and specifically targets cancer cells. REQORSA is designed to deliver the functioning TUSC2 gene to negatively charged cancer cells while minimizing uptake by normal tissue. Laboratory studies conducted at MD Anderson show that the uptake of TUSC2 in tumor cells in vitro after REQORSA treatment was 10 to 33 times the uptake in normal cells.


**About Genprex, Inc.**


Genprex, Inc. is a clinical-stage gene therapy company focusing on developing innovative treatments designed to restore biological functions disrupted by disease. The Company’s lead oncology program, Reqorsa® (quaratusugene ozeplasmid), a gene therapy product, is being developed for the treatment of lung cancer and is designed to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene to help restore tumor-suppressive activity and address multiple pathways involved in cancer progression.


The Company’s lead candidate, REQORSA, uses the systemic, non-viral ONCOPREX® Delivery System to deliver the TUSC2 tumor suppressor gene via a non-viral lipid-based nanoparticle. REQORSA is being evaluated in the Acclaim-1 and Acclaim-3 clinical trials for non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer, respectively. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track Designation to both lung cancer programs and Orphan Drug designation to the small cell lung cancer program.


Genprex is also advancing an earlier stage gene therapy program for diabetes, designed to restore insulin-producing capability through the expression of key pancreatic transcription factors. Across its programs, Genprex is focused on translating innovative gene therapy approaches into meaningful therapeutic advances for patients with significant unmet medical needs.
